subject: Dedicated GPU reservation questionnaire: workload profiling & throughput targets
messages:
From: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@acmeai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmeai.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU reservation questionnaire: workload profiling & throughput targets

Hi Vivek —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and infra ops here at Acme AI want to get a clearer picture of how Redwood recommends sizing for our expected steady-state and burst windows. We're working on an RFP but want to collect a few data points first so the numbers in the RFP are realistic.

Can you provide a completed version of the attached questionnaire that includes:
- Recommended GPU families and quant profiles for a mixed workload (LLM chat + embeddings + batch ranking)
- Expected throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec) by GPU type for 8k and 32k context lengths
- Tail latency expectations at P95/P99 under 5/20/50% slot utilization
- Guidance on reservation slotting and recommended burst buffers for seasonal peaks
- Any constraints for private deployments (VPC/HSM) that change sizing assumptions

We're attaching a workload snapshot (acme_workload_snapshot.csv) — the second tab has a sample production day. If you could get an initial pass back by Tuesday that'd be great; procurement is trying to align budgets for Q3.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lewis
Head of Infrastructure, Acme AI
procurement@acmeai.com

Attachments: acme_workload_snapshot.csv (csv)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@acmeai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU reservation questionnaire: workload profiling & throughput targets

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the snapshot and the clear ask. We're happy to run a focused sizing pass. I've attached an initial completed workbook (redwood_capacity_answer_sheet.xlsx) with conservative and aggressive sizing rows based on the CSV you provided. High-level notes up front:

- Recommended GPU families: for your mixed workload we suggest a split between A100-class (for high-concurrency embedding and batching) and H100-class (for chat + long-context 32k). For cost-sensitive path we include a quantized 4-bit option for H100 variants.
- Throughput: see tab 'throughput_summary' — approximate tokens/sec at 8k: H100-80GB (non-quantized) ~ 85-110 tok/s (per card), H100-quantized ~ 60-75 tok/s; A100-40GB for batch embeddings ~ 220-280 reqs/s (small payloads).
- Tail latency: the workbook models P95/P99 at several slot utilizations. Short answer: at 20% slot occupancy your P99 for chat with 8k stays ~250-420ms depending on model family; at 32k expect P99 increases by ~1.5-2x without KV cache hit improvements.
- Reservation slotting: we propose a three-tier slotting strategy (baseline reserved, commuter burst pool, and emergency spare). You can reserve baseline for expected 60% of steady load and rely on burst buffers for peak windows.
- Private deploy notes: VPC setups generally add <2-7ms depending on network fabric; HSM integration affects startup latency for key exchange but not per-token runtime.

Proposed next steps: quick 30-minute workshop this week to confirm model variants and risk tolerances, then we’ll finalize a runbook and commit sizing. Are you available Wed 10:30–11:00 PT?

Thanks — looping in Priyom and Monica from our Capacity and Solutions teams for the detailed sizing review.

Best,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_capacity_answer_sheet.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@acmeai.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU reservation questionnaire: workload profiling & throughput targets

Hi team —

Following Vivek's initial pass, I've run the workload snapshot through our detailed profiler and attached the model profiles (throughput_model_profiles.json) and a short runbook summary (reservation_runbook_summary.pdf). Key changes after profiling:

- We recommend shifting ~18% of baseline embedding traffic to a pre-warmed A100 pool to reduce P99 spikes during ingest-heavy minutes.
- For chat with long context (32k), set a soft cap on max concurrent sessions per H100 card and enable KV prefix caching for >=60% of sessions — this improves effective throughput by ~25-30%.
- Burst buffer sizing: for a one-day seasonal surge (x3 baseline for 6 hours) we model a conditional burst pool equal to ~30% of the baseline reserved capacity. This keeps P99 within your 1s target in our sims.

I've embedded a couple of simulation snippets in the runbook; the attached JSON includes model/sequence length distributions we used. If these assumptions map to your production traffic, the workbook's 'aggressive' row should be safe for Q3 commit.

Also, looping in Ben Carter from Sales to coordinate commercial terms if the numbers look good.

On the workshop: Wed 10:30 PT works for me. I'll bring playback slides and a short tolerance matrix for tail latency vs cost tradeoffs.

—Priyom
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: throughput_model_profiles.json (application/json); reservation_runbook_summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@acmeai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmeai.com, ops@acmeai.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU reservation questionnaire: workload profiling & throughput targets

Vivek / Priyom / Monica —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the detailed attachments. Procurement and infra ops reviewed the workbook and the runbook; the proposed baseline/aggressive rows give us the visibility we need to draft internal budget asks. A few quick items:

- We want the final runbook to include an explicit rollback/fallback plan if observed P99 > 1.5s post-cutover. Can you add a short section with the automated fallback rules you recommend?
- Please provide a short commercial note on how burst billing would be handled (metering granularity for burst pool usage).
- We're ready to schedule the workshop for Wed 10:30 PT — please send the calendar invite.

If the workshop aligns, procurement will open a formal RFP and we will follow with an expected PO in July. HubSpot link below for the deal record.

Thanks,
Sarah
Head of Infrastructure, Acme AI
